summary: Столп 4 P0 (движок, upstream-фикс, разблокирует T-0638): choros.job.instance_id/process_def_id (миграция 111, T-0534) пишутся в БД корректно при enqueue агентского job (externalTaskBridge.ts передаёт Flowable ExternalTask engine-метаданные — processInstanceId/processDefinitionKey, НЕ бизнес-переменные — как позиционные аргументы pgJobStore.enqueue()), но нигде не читались обратно. Три разрыва одной цепочки: (1) src/core/types.ts's Job-интерфейс не имел полей instanceId/processDefId вообще; (2) src/core/postgres/pgJobStore.ts's fetchAndLock() RETURNING-список и rowToJob() их не выбирали/не мапили; (3) src/server/agent-dispatch-loop.ts's PostgresAgentJobFetcher — ОТДЕЛЬНАЯ ручная копия той же CTE, РЕАЛЬНЫЙ production-путь живого агентского диспетчера (wired в main.ts, НЕ через PostgresJobStore.fetchAndLock) — имел ТУ ЖЕ дыру в своём собственном RETURNING; а downstream (4) agent-step-context.ts::readJobVars() читал instanceId/procKey ИСКЛЮЧИТЕЛЬНО из job.variables (BPMN business-переменные шага), которые никогда не несут реальный instanceId (это engine-метаданные, не process-переменная) — поэтому каждый живой agentTask давал ctx.instanceId="". Итог, вскрытый LIVE_PROOF T-0638 (репро на стенде, инстанс 99573238): T-0638's фикс defer-resolve технически корректен, но был ИНЕРТЕН — пустая строка трактуется deferred-inbox-store.ts как null → человек, завершающий взятую defer-карточку, получал 404 DEFER_NOT_ROUTABLE; инстанс висел, хотя движок токен давно продвинул. ФИКС (после релокации по R-1, см. ниже): протянуты обе DB-колонки (уже существующие с миграции 111 — 0 новых миграций) через НЕ-замороженные звенья (types.ts, pgJobStore.ts, agent-dispatch-loop.ts); значение впрыскивается в job.variables на НЕЗАМОРОЖЕННОМ call-site (agent-dispatch-loop.ts's PostgresAgentJobFetcher) под теми же ключами (instanceId/procKey), которые ЗАМОРОЖЕННЫЙ readJobVars() и так читает — поэтому frozen-файл agent-step-context.ts НЕ трогается вовсе, а readJobVars находит значение через свой существующий variables-lookup. Аддитивно и обратно совместимо: InMemoryJobStore не менялся; legacy/NULL-колонки → впрыск пропускается, variables-fallback сохраняется.

review_response.why_the_false_pass_happened: The earlier PASS reading was taken against an UNCOMMITTED working tree: FF-15 computes `git diff --name-only $(git merge-base HEAD dev)...HEAD`, which only sees COMMITTED changes. At the time I ran the gate, HEAD was still at dev@ed75608 (my edits were unstaged), so dev...HEAD was empty → PASS. Once committed, FF-15 deterministically FAILs. This was a real process error on my part — I asserted a gate result without re-running it against the committed state. The corrected handoff below never claims a gate passed unless it was run against the committed HEAD.
review_response.resolution: Option (b) — relocation, NOT a freeze crossing (no sign-off obtainable from this isolated worktree, and per founder memory T-0586/T-0587 are open/blocked, so the freeze is live). Reverted src/runtime/agent-dispatch/agent-step-context.ts and its test byte-for-byte back to dev (readJobVars() untouched/frozen). Moved the instanceId/procKey injection to the NON-frozen call site (src/server/agent-dispatch-loop.ts's PostgresAgentJobFetcher.fetchAndLockAgentJobs, where __tenantId is already stamped): the migration-111 column values are written into job.variables under the SAME keys the frozen readJobVars() already probes (`instanceId` / `procKey`), so readJobVars returns the real value with ZERO edits to the frozen file. Relocated the readJobVars coverage from the frozen unit-test file to the non-frozen DB-integration test (ci/checks/db/agent-dispatch-cross-tenant.test.ts), which exercises the REAL PostgresAgentJobFetcher and asserts variables.instanceId/procKey injection + override/fallback semantics. R-2 (nit) also addressed: added two isolated enqueue()-return-value tests in pgJobStore.integration.test.ts.
review_response.net_diff_is_clean: `git diff --name-only dev...HEAD` after the relocation commit contains NO src/runtime/agent-dispatch/ path. Verified `bash ci/checks/agent-bridge-contract.sh` now exits 0 with `PASS [FF-15]: diff vs ed75608... does not touch any T-0586/T-0587/T-0588 owned path`.

mechanism.root_cause: Migration 111 (T-0534, tel-intake DMN triage seam) added choros.job.process_def_id/instance_id specifically so the triage seam could scope rule-table lookups by process WITHOUT relying on process variables (migration docstring's own stated intent). externalTaskBridge.ts's runBridgeOnce already passes task.processDefinitionKey/task.processInstanceId (real Flowable ExternalTask wire-shape fields, src/core/flowable-client.ts) into pgJobStore.enqueue()'s 5th/6th positional params, which correctly INSERTs them. But no code downstream ever selected them back: pgJobStore.ts's JobRow interface/rowToJob()/fetchAndLock() RETURNING clause omitted the columns entirely; src/core/types.ts's Job interface had no processDefId/instanceId fields at all. Separately AND MORE CRITICALLY, the actual live agent-dispatch loop (main.ts wires startAgentDispatchLoop, which constructs PostgresAgentJobFetcher, src/server/agent-dispatch-loop.ts:545) does NOT call PostgresJobStore.fetchAndLock at all — it has its OWN hand-rolled fetchAndLock-equivalent CTE (necessitated by the migrator/BYPASSRLS cross-tenant discovery logic PostgresJobStore.fetchAndLock doesn't implement), with an independently-authored RETURNING list that had the identical omission. Downstream, agent-step-context.ts's readJobVars() (the frozen file) reads instanceId/procKey ONLY from job.variables via candidate-key probing (str("instanceId")||str("processInstanceId")||str("inst") and str("procKey")||str("processKey")||str("proc_key")) — but job.variables holds BPMN business variables (task.variables from the Flowable external task), and no code stamps a variables.instanceId/procKey entry for a live agent-step job. Result: every freshly-dispatched agentTask job produced ctx.instanceId==='' — exactly the symptom T-0638's live-proof captured (repro instance 99573238, stand http://100.121.76.86:3000).
mechanism.fix_chosen: Threaded the ALREADY-CORRECT enqueue-time values through the read points WITHOUT editing the frozen agent-step-context.ts (post-R-1 relocation): (1) src/core/types.ts (NOT frozen) — Job gains `processDefId?: string | null` and `instanceId?: string | null`, both OPTIONAL so every existing Job-literal construction site keeps compiling unmodified. (2) src/core/postgres/pgJobStore.ts (NOT frozen) — JobRow gains matching optional snake_case fields; rowToJob() maps them with a `?? null` normalization; EVERY SELECT/RETURNING list in the file (both enqueue paths, getById, listByTopic, listByState, listByTopicAndState, and the critical fetchAndLock) now explicitly lists process_def_id, instance_id. (3) src/server/agent-dispatch-loop.ts (NOT frozen — NOT in the FF-15 forbidden list) — PostgresAgentJobFetcher's own inlined CTE RETURNING gains j.process_def_id/j.instance_id, the inline TS row-type gains matching fields, AND — the key relocation move — the jobRows.map(...) construction INJECTS the column values into job.variables under the keys the frozen readJobVars() probes (`instanceId`, `procKey`), alongside the existing __tenantId stamping. Spread order is `...r.variables` first, then the injected keys override when the migration-111 column is non-empty (the engine-captured id wins over a stale same-named business var), then __tenantId last; a NULL/empty column skips the injection so a legacy job's own variables.instanceId is preserved. The Job object also carries the top-level processDefId/instanceId (belt to the variables suspenders — useful for DB assertions / future non-frozen consumers). (4) agent-step-context.ts::readJobVars() — UNCHANGED (reverted to dev byte-for-byte); it finds the injected value through its pre-existing, un-edited variables lookup.
mechanism.not_weakening: No migration added (columns exist since 111 — pure code-thread, zero DDL). No frozen file touched: agent-step-context.ts and its test are byte-identical to dev (git diff dev -- src/runtime/agent-dispatch/ = 0 lines); no ci/checks/*.sh file edited (frozen-checks-immutable.sh not applicable — no shell-gate change). FF-15 (T-0586/T-0587/T-0588 zone) now PASSes because the net dev...HEAD diff no longer touches src/runtime/agent-dispatch/. anti-case-lock.sh stays at its exact pre-existing baseline (new test literals telLinear/procA/procB live in *.test.ts files, excluded by the gate's own test-file exclusion rule — verified via anti-case-lock.sh --self-test). flowable-bridge-contract.sh and agent-bridge-contract.sh both verified green against the committed HEAD post-relocation. ACCEPTED DECISION 1 (dispatch-outcome.ts's defer-always-closes semantics) untouched — this task only fixes what ctx.instanceId CONTAINS.
mechanism.side_effects_checked: InMemoryJobStore (src/core/inMemoryJobStore.ts) audited: its enqueue() is a 3-parameter method that does NOT accept processDefId/instanceId (T-0534's extension only exists on PostgresJobStore.enqueue) — jobs it produces simply lack these optional Job fields, and readJobVars() falls through to the (unchanged) variables-based fallback for them. No other Job-literal construction site in src/ needs updating (only inMemoryJobStore.ts and a single field-only type-cast in agent-dispatch-loop.ts, both safe). enqueue()'s own RETURNING lists (both plain and idempotent-conflict) were updated for completeness/consistency and are now covered by two isolated enqueue-return-value tests (R-2). The variables-injection override semantics (DB column wins over a stale same-named business var; NULL column preserves legacy variables value) are covered by dedicated DB-integration tests.

chain_threaded: enqueue (src/core/externalTaskBridge.ts, unchanged — already wrote process_def_id/instance_id correctly to the DB via pgJobStore.enqueue()'s positional 5th/6th args, sourced from Flowable ExternalTask.processDefinitionKey/processInstanceId) → choros.job DB columns (migration 111, unchanged, already correct) → src/core/postgres/pgJobStore.ts's fetchAndLock/enqueue/getById/listBy* RETURNING+SELECT lists (FIXED, non-frozen: now select process_def_id, instance_id) → rowToJob() (FIXED, non-frozen: maps them onto Job.processDefId/instanceId with ?? null) → src/server/agent-dispatch-loop.ts's PostgresAgentJobFetcher.fetchAndLockAgentJobs — the REAL production path (FIXED, non-frozen: RETURNING + row-type + jobRows.map() which now (a) stamps top-level Job.processDefId/instanceId AND (b) INJECTS them into job.variables under keys `instanceId`/`procKey`) → src/runtime/agent-dispatch/agent-step-context.ts::readJobVars() (UNCHANGED/FROZEN — reads variables.instanceId/procKey via its pre-existing lookup, now finds the injected value) → assembleAgentStepContext's AgentStepContext.instanceId/procKey (unchanged, now receives a real value) → dispatch-outcome.ts's deferredAuditEvent's payload.instance_id (unchanged) → deferred-inbox-store.ts's DeferredInboxRow.instanceId (unchanged, T-0638) → POST /api/inbox/:id/action's resolve-by-instance engine-drive (unchanged, T-0638) — the whole downstream mechanism T-0638 built is now fed a real value instead of "".
call_site_injection: The instanceId/processDefId are injected in src/server/agent-dispatch-loop.ts, inside PostgresAgentJobFetcher.fetchAndLockAgentJobs's jobRows.map(...) — the same non-frozen block that already stamps variables.__tenantId. They are written into job.variables under keys `instanceId` and `procKey`, which are exactly the first candidate keys the (frozen, un-edited) agent-step-context.ts::readJobVars() probes. This is why the frozen file needs no change: readJobVars reads variables.instanceId, and the call site now populates it. Spread order `{...r.variables, ...(column ? {instanceId: col} : {}), ...(column ? {procKey: col} : {}), __tenantId}` makes the engine-captured migration-111 column override a stale same-named business variable, while a NULL column skips the injection entirely so a legacy job's own variables.instanceId survives (readJobVars fallback preserved).
in_memory_jobstore: src/core/inMemoryJobStore.ts audited, NOT modified, NOT broken. Its enqueue() is a 3-parameter method (no processDefId/instanceId params — that extension only exists on PostgresJobStore.enqueue's 7-parameter signature). Job objects it constructs use an explicit object literal; adding two OPTIONAL fields to the Job interface does not require it to populate them. readJobVars() for in-memory-driven jobs falls through cleanly to the pre-existing variables-based lookup, unchanged behavior.

deviations_from_adr: ADR-T0677 §2.4 originally described editing readJobVars() in agent-step-context.ts to prefer job.instanceId/job.processDefId. After R-1 (FF-15 frozen-zone), the fix was RELOCATED: readJobVars() is now untouched/frozen, and the same authoritative value is injected into job.variables at the non-frozen call site (agent-dispatch-loop.ts) under the keys readJobVars already reads. friction_events: PROCESS ERROR (root of R-1's false-PASS): I ran `bash ci/checks/agent-bridge-contract.sh` and recorded PASS while my changes were still UNCOMMITTED. FF-15 diffs `git merge-base HEAD dev...HEAD`, which only sees committed changes — with HEAD still at dev, the diff was empty and the gate trivially passed. Once committed, FF-15 deterministically FAILed (`diff touches forbidden zone path: src/runtime/agent-dispatch/`). Lesson: diff-based gates MUST be run against the committed HEAD, not the working tree. All gate results in this corrected handoff were run post-commit.

This task required auditing TWO independent RETURNING/SELECT implementations of the same fetchAndLock CTE (PostgresJobStore.fetchAndLock AND PostgresAgentJobFetcher's inlined CTE) — the T-0638 handoff's follow_up only named 'pgJobStore.ts's fetchAndLock', which would NOT have fixed the actual production path (main.ts wires PostgresAgentJobFetcher). Traced main.ts → startAgentDispatchLoop → PostgresAgentJobFetcher (line 545) to confirm both call sites needed the fix.

The readJobVars() fix genuinely lives in a frozen file (agent-step-context.ts, FF-15 zone for in-flight T-0586/T-0587/T-0588). Rather than cross the freeze (no sign-off obtainable from this worktree; the zone-owning tasks are open/blocked), the fix was relocated to inject the corrected value at the non-frozen call site under the exact keys the frozen reader already probes — a zero-freeze-crossing solution. The frozen file and its test were reverted to dev byte-for-byte.
